description: A chief legal officer must approve a proposed trademark coexistence agreement with a competitor and set the protected fields, territorial reservation, no-challenge protection, and domain-transfer condition, with input from trademark counsel, the product liaison, and corporate records counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company owns a registered NOVA trademark, and a competitor has applied to register NOVA for goods that appear adjacent to the company's products.
shared_context.S2: The competitor has proposed resolving the matter through a coexistence agreement instead of a contested opposition.
shared_context.S3: The proposed agreement would let the parties define their respective product fields and other operating restrictions before the competitor's application proceeds.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard approval routine, Elena asks trademark, product, and corporate-records counsel to identify any terms that must be addressed before she approves the agreement.

PF1.text: Thomas reviewed the archived 2018 settlement with the competitor's parent and confirmed that the agreed boundary reserves industrial controls to this company and permits the other side to use NOVA only for residential lighting; the new agreement must state that boundary and include a mutual no-challenge clause. He found the signed settlement while checking the old opposition file, but has not circulated it to Elena.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the product team this week that the company will launch NOVA Grid industrial-controls products in Germany and needs its industrial-controls reservation to apply worldwide, including Germany; the team will not approve a Germany carve-out. Her launch notes remain in the product team's workspace.

PF3.text: Victor checked the competitor's corporate-domain records and confirmed that the competitor controls nova-grid.com, which it has offered to transfer to this company as a condition of signing; the agreement must require transfer of that domain at execution. He completed the check for the signing checklist, which has not yet been updated.

acceptance_conditions: The coexistence agreement must be approved.
The agreement must include a mutual no-challenge clause.
The competitor's field must be limited to residential lighting only.
The company's reserved field must be industrial controls.
The company's industrial-controls reservation must apply worldwide.
The agreement must require transfer of nova-grid.com at execution.
The archived 2018 settlement must be cited as justification for the field boundary and no-challenge clause.

decisive_facts.why: The archived settlement changes the agreement from an undefined coexistence arrangement to one requiring a mutual no-challenge clause, a residential-lighting-only competitor field, and an industrial-controls reservation for the company.
The confirmed NOVA Grid launch in Germany changes the territorial reservation from an unspecified or limited territory to a worldwide reservation that includes Germany.
The domain-record check changes the execution package by requiring transfer of the specifically named nova-grid.com domain to the company at signing.
